claims.statement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 requires, from 18 February 2027, a battery passport for each LMT battery, EV battery, and industrial battery above 2 kWh, with model- and unit-specific access tiers.
The regulation permits authorized processors to store passport data on behalf of the responsible operator but restricts selling, reusing, or processing it beyond the service purpose.

contrary_evidence: Large battery OEMs can bundle passports, and the regulation's reuse restriction sharply limits any cross-customer data moat.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a permissioned library of OEM field mappings, validation failures, and lifecycle workflows lowers onboarding cost while each customer retains its data rights
fingerprint.customer: small EU stationary-storage importers and installers lacking an internal product-data infrastructure
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: storage distributors, conformity consultants, and renewable installers embed issuance in their commissioning workflow
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: delegated passport issuance, role-based access, lifecycle updates, and audit export sold per asset plus custody subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the responsible importer or brand owner pays when each passport is issued and annually while the record is maintained
fingerprint.problem_trigger: an industrial battery above 2 kWh is about to be placed on the EU market or put into service under the passport rule

founder_fit: Strong data-engineering and renewable-channel fit; can begin with the family installation network and avoid public-facing marketing. Use only customer-authorized data.
risks: Incorrect passport data could create contractual or regulatory liability.
A common free industry platform could compress pricing.

structure.control_point: creation and custody of the compliant QR-linked battery record at EU market placement or commissioning
structure.critical_dependency: economic-operator authorization plus stable technical standards and OEM access to required model- and unit-level data

thesis: Operate the delegated QR identity, access-control, and lifecycle-record layer for EU importers and installers of stationary batteries above the regulated capacity threshold. The narrow wedge is the passport issued when a battery is placed on the market or put into service; customer-authorized lifecycle records then create switching costs without claiming ownership of protected OEM data. All commercial numbers, including capital_required_pln, are unvalidated hypotheses.
title: Battery Passport Issuance Rail for Independent Storage Importers
